author: allan2
body:
This commit splits _tlk.ps1_. It strives to make certain parts easier to run and to make the building and packaging process more readable.

The documentation of how to use the new scripts is in [_ci/README.md_](https://github.com/Devolutions/devolutions-gateway/blob/e98ef1a3368cffc352d9cae0183051adabd31945/ci/README.md). The existing _tlk.ps1_ is untouched as this PR does not include integration with GitHub Actions.

- usage is more strict; unsupported configurations (building on supported platforms, unused arguments) will throw an error
- _build.ps1_ now uses the `target/profile` build by default, without having to build into a separate target/arch folder
- architecture is an optional parameter for _build.ps1_, detecting your system architecture if not specified
- output directory structure now uses the full target triplet
  - this is to enable building for additional targets in the future such as musl
- removed `cargo test` functionality
- removed unused verbosed flag in `TlkRecipe`
- removed unused `Get-DotEnvFile` function
- removed DGATEWAY_PSMODULE_CLEAN functionality
- fail with `Stop` instead of `SilentlyContinue` when copying files
- use of named parameters for the PS scripts instead of environment variables
  - this makes it clear up-front what is required when building or packaging a given product
  - in the future, I would like to pass more parameters to `MSBuild` as properties instead of through environment variables
- functions are named using PowerShell-approved verbs
- adds documentation

This commit contains all scripts for building on all platforms and packaging on Windows.

author: christian-photo
body:
- ⚠️ **Breaking** `image/{index}` now includes more images. Every image that is recieved as a websocket event can now be loaded using this endpoint. This is because the `imageType`
  parameter was introduced. The endpoint doesn't use NINA's image history anymore, but instead uses the websocket history. This includes more images and will result in a more consistent experience.
  The issue with NINA's image history is, that it does not necessarily include all images, like calibration frames.

### Flats

- Added the following methods for capturing flats:
  - `flats/skyflat`
  - `flats/auto-brightness`
  - `flats/auto-exposure`
  - `flats/trained-dark-flat`
  - `flats/trained-flat`

These methods do exactly the same as their sequence instruction counterparts.

- Added `flats/status` to get the status of the flat taking process.
- Added `flats/stop` to stop the flat taking process.

### Mount

- Added `waitForResult` to `mount/slew` to wait for the slew to finish.
- Added `mount/slew/stop` to abort the current slew.
- Added a `mount` websocket channel to move the mount axis manually. This automatically stops all movement when the client disconnects as a safety measure to prevent any accidents.

### Image

- Added `imageType` to `image/{index}` and `image-history` to filter the images by type.
- Added `debayer` and `bayerPattern` to `image/{index}` to debayer the image.
- Added `IsBayered` to `IMAGE-SAVE` event (and `image-history`).
- Added `autoPrepare` to `image/{index}` to leave all processing up to NINA. Using this will result in the same image as the one you see in NINA

---

- Added `PROFILE-ADDED` and `PROFILE-REMOVED` events to get notified when the collection of profiles changes, `PROFILE-CHANGED` is sent when the active profile changes.

author: grpinto
body:
Description of changes

I have benchmarked the initial part of DIALOGUE (DIALOGUE1). I changed the _pseudobulk_feature_space function so that the user can choose the aggregation method (median or mean) and the output now has samples as rows, matching the R implementation. I also modified the _scale_data function to center, scale, and cap extreme values (with a cap of 0.01) in a way that mirrors the R functions center.matrix and cap.mat. In addition, I updated the _load function to optionally restrict the data to common samples across cell types. The output of _load is now a dataframe that is converted back to a numpy array before further processing.

Technical details

The changes make the pseudobulk and normalization steps in Python produce results that match the R version. I added an optional parameter to subset to common samples and to choose the averaging function. I also ensure that the data are converted to numpy arrays before passing them to the penalized matrix decomposition functions.

Additional context

These changes only affect the initial part of DIALOGUE (DIALOGUE1) and do not modify downstream analysis.

author: rushilmehra
body: Previously, set_ech_keys would consume the SslEchKeys struct to enforce the requirement that the struct is immutable after initializing it on a SSL_CTX. The problem with this is that it requires applications to needlessly reallocate the SslEchKeys struct if they want to initialize keys on multiple SSL_CTXs, which is a pretty common pattern. To work around this, we introduce a builder (SslEchKeysBuilder) that requires mutable access to add keys to the underlying struct. set_ech_keys takes in a reference to SslEchKeys, which can only be made via consuming the builder.

author: revise-dev[bot]
body:
The error occurs because the ROI calculator is attempting to divide by `investment_length_in_years` which can become `nil` when empty values are submitted through the form. The original code in `ToolFloat#cast` removes non-numeric characters and attempts to cast the value to a float, but when given an empty string or nil input, it returns nil instead of a default value. This causes issues in calculations like `(roi / investment_length_in_years).round(2)` where `investment_length_in_years` becomes nil, resulting in the TypeError: "nil can't be coerced into Float". The fix modifies the `ToolFloat#cast` method to provide a default value of 0.0 when the input is blank. We use `value.presence || 0.0` which: 1. Returns nil if the value is blank (empty string, nil, or only whitespace) 2. Returns the value itself if it's present 3. Falls back to 0.0 if the value was blank This maintains the original intent of the code (converting string inputs to floats) while adding proper handling for blank inputs, preventing nil from propagating into calculations. The change is safe because: - It preserves all existing numeric parsing functionality - It maintains type consistency by always returning a float - It matches the default value of 0.0 specified in the RoiCalculator presenter's attributes - It prevents division by zero errors by allowing subsequent validation logic to catch zero values

body:
This PR creates the option (`max_res_in_ocn=True`) to maintain the highest resolution used on land ice cells in all ocean cells when generating the GIS MALI mesh. This is done to resolve fjord geometry and coastal bathymetry necessary to translate ocean properties to glacier termini when coupling MALI to MPAS-Ocean (or prescribing ocean forcing to MALI in standalone mode). As this has the potential to drastically increase mesh generation time, so there is an additional option `define_bnds_by_geojson=True` that performs an initial cull of the BedMachine dataset according to the bounds set by `compass/landice/tests/greenland/gis_contShelfExtent_PS.geojson` before generating the mesh in Jigsaw.

This PR has been tested with both the Greenland and Uummannaq/Disko mesh gen test cases

author: jaxesn
body:
*Issue #, if available:*

*Description of changes:*

There are multiple levels of cleanup in our e2e test.  The normal testing flow goes like:

- e2e-test setup... to create the Infra CFN Stack and the EKS Cluster, along with a handful of other resources
- ginkgo run... runs a single (or multiple tests in parallel), either way at the beginning on such a run, the Credential CFN Stack is created, along other resources such as the  access entries
- when a test completes, it cleans up the EC2 instance associated with that test
- when all the tests complete, the cred cfn stack is deleted, along with the access entry and other resources
- in ci, e2e-test cleanup is than ran to delete the eks cluster and then the infra stack
- at the end of the ci run (and beginning), we also run the e2e_cleanup.sh script to catch any potential orphaned resources

Currently, ssm activations and managed instances are the only (there could be another i am forgetting) resources that are not cleaned up by the e2e-test/gingko assuming everything completes successfully.

This PR adds activation/managed instance cleanup to tests themselves which would mean if everything works correctly, the bash script will not do anything.

We should think of this current bash script as a failsafe to clean up anything our test cleanup and/or cloudformation leaves around.  We want to keep this process.  That said, this PR also starts the process of moving this logic into go to better fit the rest of the code base and reuse as much as possible.  There are 3 use cases for this new cleanup flow, which match more or less how we use the bash script today:
- cleanup with a specific cluster name. this is run at the end of a CI build or Canary run and it deletes everything associated with that cluster regardless of its age
- cleanup with a cluster name prefix. this is run at the beginning of a canary run for a specific kube version, ex: nodeadm-e2e-1-31-, this will delete all clusters and resources with that prefix regardless of their age
- cleanup with no cluster prefix/name, this is run currently at the beginning of a ci run and intended to delete all clusters a day old

This PR models these use cases with flags on the e2e-test cleanup subcommand.

body:
# Overview
As I'm going through cleaning up the website's icons, I'm realizing the media queries are in desperate need of some attention. Instead of trying to tie it all in together in one messy PR, I thought I'd break it out to a separate PR.

## Media query changes
There were two files where media queries were being created:
- `src/reusable/media-queries.js` (removed in favor of using the media queries in utils.js)
- `src/reusable/utils.js` (moved media queries from /reusable/media-queries.js to this file)

Three files had local media query declaration that were removed and replaced with media queries from utils:
- `src/components/panels/group-panel.js`
- `src/components/panels/hero-search-box.js`
- `src/components/panels/hero-text.js`

Removing the media-queries.js file required some restructure of the media queries, specifically the 620px media query (previously referred to as `MEDIA_QUERIES.LARGESCREEN`). In moving the media queries from media-queries.js, this become the smallest breakpoint so it was renamed to `MEDIA_QUERIES.S`. The `MEDIA_QUERIES.SMALLSCREEN` breakpoint at 320px was not used so it was removed.

Finally, there are media queries defined specifically for the header in `src/components/header/header-media-queries.js` the define the breakpoint for the header to collapse. This is set to a fixed pixel width that is the exact max-width of the container before content wraps. As the navigation changes, this should be updated to swap between the mobile / collapsed version as needed.

## Testing
- Make sure the PR is consistent in these browsers at different resolutions:
  - [x] Chrome
  - [x] Firefox

author: jgallagher
body:
Fixes #7363.

I was able to reproduce this locally by making MGS sleep between starting its Oximeter server and starting to collect metrics from SPs:

```diff
+++ b/gateway/src/metrics.rs
@@ -427,6 +427,7 @@ async fn start_pollers(
     .await
     .context("we should never return a fatal error here")?;

+    tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(20)).await;
     slog::info!(
         &log,
         "starting to poll SP sensor data every {SP_POLL_INTERVAL:?}"
```

With that sleep injected and the changes in this PR, the test takes ~30 seconds instead of ~10 seconds, but still passes.

author: alopez-suse
body:
This PR implements a fixed registry type for the GitHub Container Registry, which allows a user to set `namespace/*` filters when scanning.

The generic `*` filter is not allowed when scanning the GitHub container registry, as it would scan every package visible to the scanning user on the GitHub Container Registry. While I could have limited the `*` filter to use the given username as a namespace, I prefer the unambiguous behavior of just disallowing the filter. Instead, the user can use a filter such as `rancher/*` to scan every package visible to the user under the Rancher namespace.

The GitHub registry API seems to differentiate between "users" and "organizations" endpoints (referred to here as namespaces) even though the behavior is exactly the same for both of them. Also, a "user" and an "organization" cannot share the same name, so in my implementation, instead of requiring the user to specify whether they are scanning an "organization" or "user" I just try the organization endpoint first, and fallback to the user endpoint in the case of a "not found" error.

author: say-yawn
body:
According to the co-founder of Prometheus counters should not be used as an absolute value as it does not account for when the metric is reset ([video](https://youtu.be/fhx0ehppMGM?t=237)):

> Coming to PromQL again, you'll almost never want to look at the absolute value of a counter. If you think about it, counters are just cumulative counts over some arbitrary amount of time that totally depends on when the counter start from zero ... And the absolute value doesn't tell you anything useful at all.

So I'm testing the data with gauge to see it handles the metric reset better. I'm also [reading](https://iximiuz.com/en/posts/prometheus-functions-agg-over-time/) that `sum_over_time()` works better with gauges which is what we want to do instead of going sampling the sum of the increase (instant vector) which is what `sum by(namespace, keyid, user) (autograph_signer_requests{namespace=~"autograph-$env"}[$__rate_interval])` seem to be doing.

Fix AUT-393

body:
## Summary & Motivation

Sensors are supposed to skip subsequent `RunRequests` that have the same run key as a previous run. This works across ticks but not for `RunRequests` within the same tick-- currently two runs will be launched with the same key from within the same tick.

This PR amends the sensor daemon logic to ensure that sensor `RunRequests` with the same run key are handled the same as they are across runs.

User @Gw1p submitted an initial attempt [here](https://github.com/dagster-io/dagster/pull/27322) at fixing this but an alternative approach was required to ensure identical handling of cross-tick and same-tick duplicates.

## How I Tested These Changes

New unit test.

## Changelog

Fixed a bug where a sensor emitting multiple `RunRequests` with the same run key within a single tick would cause two runs with the same key to be executed. Now only the first run will be executed.

Co-authored by: Anton <20753476+Gw1p@users.noreply.github.com>

author: lmcorbalan
body:
### Issue
A vulnerability was identified that allowed malicious users to trigger a refund on a chain where the order was never intended to be filled. This exploit enabled attackers to illicitly obtain the solver’s payment when an order was filled but not properly settled before the attack.

This could be reproduced by:
1. User open order from chain 1 with chain 2 as destination 
2. Filler calls `fill` on chain 2 for the user order
3. Order fillDeadline expired and filler hasn't call `settle` on chain 2 for user yet
4. User calls `refund` on chain 3, since the order id has not been filled in chain 3 it sends an the refund interchain message to chain 1
5. The interchain message is refunden since order status is still OPEN

### Remedy 
It prevents miss-refunding an order by validating that the interchain message origin is the same as the `order.destinationChain` when handling the refund message

author: romerojosh
body:
On systems with multi-node NVLink (MNNVL) capabilities, fast communication can occur via NVLink between GPUs that are on separate nodes. The existing pipelined all-to-all communication ordering in cuDecomp makes an attempt to hide faster P2P transfers over NVLink behind slower transfers over IB, but the existing logic was designed with the assumption that NVLink connections only exist with intra-node peers.

This PR generalizes the communication scheduling logic to treat MNNVL "cliques" (i.e. a group of GPUs connected with NVLink) as a logical "node". This enables cuDecomp to pair up "inter-clique" NVLink communications with "inter-clique" IB communication to generalize the communication hiding optimization to MNNVL systems. To detect MNNVL support and clique assignments, bindings to the NVIDIA management library (NVML) have been added in this PR.

When adding new deposit routes, if the LP token for the given L1 token does not yet exist, create the LP token and atomically deposit and burn a single unit. This prevents the HubPool from ever having a 0 balance of the l1 token, protecting against a known issue.

It's been on the todo list to automate this for a while, but it hasn't been prioritised because adding LP tokens is quite infrequent. Atomic deposit-and-burn was done manually last time (0x566087fbaa74a32ec94bf4ba58c1451bf916991b686c0895245f726339b1725d), but it's preferable to automate this as much as possible to remove the human element.

[Pixi](https://github.com/prefix-dev/pixi) is an up-and-coming competitor to conda that uses the same packages from conda-forge (and potentially PyPI) but is much faster, easier to boostrap (it's a native executable, not a python program, so you don't need to install python to install conda to install python), has lockfile functionality that's built in (in contrast to conda-lock which is a separate package) and better, and generally seems to be a lot more stable and robust.

The immediate impetus for this change is that I had to build a new image while on the NiMet call and it took something like 20 minutes. Now with pixi it takes 1m10s.

I'm submitting this as a draft because I haven't been able to test it yet. I went through six different partners' python_maproom_* repos and couldn't find one with a config-iri.yaml that worked with the current version of enactsmaproom. We should set up a test country whose config we keep in this repo for testing and development purposes.

Server Changes:
- Server refactored to use new transport interface
- Moved start command to server subcommand
- Added request handler implementation
- Improved shutdown handling

Breaking Changes:
- Start command moved to 'server start'
- Provider interfaces now require context parameter
- Transport creation requires options pattern

Migration Guide:
- Update command usage from 'start' to 'server start'
- Pass context to provider methods
- Use transport options when creating transports

## Summary by Sourcery

This pull request enhances the FASTA parsing functionality, improves error handling and robustness of the vector database integration, and updates the plotting customizations. It also includes comprehensive unit tests for the FASTA parsing functionality.

New Features:
- Improves FASTA parsing by handling multi-line sequences, irregular spacing, and incomplete annotations.
- Adds comprehensive unit tests for FASTA parsing, covering standard formats, edge cases like empty files, and various annotation scenarios.

Bug Fixes:
- Fixes an issue where empty BRENDA entries were not handled correctly in plotting, replacing them with 'unknown' to ensure proper plotting.
- Fixes a recursion error when accessing the vector database with large datasets by increasing the recursion limit.

Enhancements:
- Updates the `custom_plotting` function to handle cases where certain columns ('xref_brenda', 'ec', 'organism_id') might be missing from the DataFrame, preventing errors.
- Improves error handling in `database_access` by raising a ValueError if the length of the DataFrame and embeddings do not match, suggesting a re-embedding.
- Improves vector database access by increasing the timeout and setting the recursion limit to avoid errors with large datasets.

Tests:

body:
Add a reproducer for the crash on a bad variant access which was fixed in commit 7d75161051da ("librbd: fix a crash in get_rollback_snap_id").

The reproducer deliberately works around many other issues with force promote in snapshot-based mirroring: stopping rbd-mirror daemon shouldn't be necessary (let alone with SIGKILL), get_rollback_snap_id() and its caller can_create_primary_snapshot() are flawed and can pick the wrong snapshot to roll back to or skip rollback when it's actually required, the user snapshot in this scenario should be removed as part of force promoting because it's incomplete and won't be usable after the image is promoted, etc.
